draft.title: Awards and enterprise agreements
card: a legal document that sets minimum pay and conditions for workers in a particular industry or occupation, such as retail or hospitality.
a set of pay and conditions negotiated by an employer and its employees at one workplace or business. It is approved by the Fair Work Commission.
An enterprise agreement must pass the better off overall test. Taken as a whole, each worker must be better off than under the award that would otherwise cover them.
An agreement can trade one entitlement for another, such as flexible hours for a different loading. It cannot leave workers worse off overall.
draft.remember: An award is the industry minimum. An agreement is made at one workplace and must beat that minimum overall.

a.q: Which statement best separates a modern award from an enterprise agreement?
opts: An award covers an industry, an agreement one workplace
An award covers one workplace, an agreement an industry
An award is negotiated by staff, an agreement is set by law
An award binds employers, an agreement binds workers
a.why: A modern award sets minimum pay and conditions across an industry. An enterprise agreement is negotiated by the employer and employees at one workplace. The reversed option is tempting, but it swaps the two.
a.clue: Think about how many workplaces each one covers.

b.q: Kiran runs a café group in Geelong and offers staff an enterprise agreement. It lifts base pay but cuts weekend loadings below the award. Which test decides if it can be approved?
opts: Whether the package as a whole beats the award
Whether each condition on its own beats the award
Whether most of the owners agree to the package
Whether its pay beats that of rival cafés nearby
b.why: The better off overall test looks at the whole package, not each item. Lower loadings can be made up for by higher base pay. Requiring each condition to beat the award is tempting, but the test does not demand it.
b.clue: Can a loss in one area be made up by a gain in another?

a.best: An award covers an industry, an agreement one workplace

b.best: Whether the package as a whole beats the award
